translation.english_title: Saying the ocean-girdled world had dawned

english_lines: Saying the ocean-girdled world had dawned,
Crowed like a rooster and even my chastity,
You pecked away, cruel woman! Great sinner!
You came here like the end-age and played havoc; broken,
I have become like a shattered thaazhi-vessel — now,
Will this life remain even one moment?
Will it state the grammar of chastity... will it...
notes: `ஆழிசூழ் உலகம்` remains the classical concrete `ocean-girdled world` rather than being reduced to `the world`.
`கற்புக்கு இலக்கணம்` is retained as `the grammar of chastity`, preserving Kalaignar's striking grammar/morality formulation.
`தாழி` is retained as `thaazhi-vessel` because a generic `pot` would flatten the culturally specific object; the source's broken-vessel comparison remains explicit.
The end-age/deluge force of `ஊழி` remains catastrophic rather than softened to `storm`.

translator_notes: The accusatory violence of crowing, pecking, chastity, end-age and broken-vessel imagery is retained without euphemism.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
